Jordan —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Attached is a first-pass redline that focuses only on term/renewal/termination language so your legal and procurement teams can review quickly. High-level proposal in the redline: 

- Base term: 12 months.
- Auto-renewal: automatic 12-month renewal unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least 60 days before the end of term.
- Termination for convenience: either party may terminate with 45 days' written notice; customer is eligible for a pro-rata refund for unused committed capacity.
- Wind-down obligations: 30-day data extraction window; temporary access for exports; standard deletion timeline after export window.

Our ask: please confirm whether 60/45/30 (notice/termination/wind-down) is workable from Acme's side or suggest alternative windows. If you prefer, we can move the auto-renew notice to 45 days and shorten termination-for-convenience to 30 days — want to capture your preference before Jade (legal) does a formal redline.

I'll loop in Karthik for a suggested fallback clause for enterprise renewals and Marcus for commercial sign-off. Would you be open to a 30-minute call on Friday to align?

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Evelyn —

Thanks for sending this over and for the clear summary. A few immediate notes from procurement/legal: 

1) Auto-renew notice: 60 days is longer than our standard procurement window for SaaS; we typically ask for 30 days but can accept 45 with internal approval. Can you do 45 as a middle ground?
2) Termination for convenience: Acme prefers a shorter notice (30 days) to preserve flexibility; our legal team is concerned about a 45-day requirement for this clause.
3) Wind-down and data extraction: we absolutely need a clear runbook in the contract for data export, export formats, and escrow if needed. Also: who bears egress costs during the export window?
4) Refunds: procurement expects a pro-rata credit; please confirm you will not charge for unused committed capacity beyond the pro-rata.

I've attached examples of notice windows from our vendor playbook for reference. I'd like to get this into our contract queue this week — can you share an alternate redline with 45/30/30 (auto-renew notice/termination/wind-down) options?

If we can't reach alignment on notice windows, our legal team may return a formal redline with different language (e.g., explicit exception for early termination in the event of security incidents).

Let's do a quick call Friday 11:00am PT if that works.

Jordan Price
Head of Procurement | Acme Financial Services
jordan.price@acmefin.com | +1 (212) 555-0198

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed termination workflow & renewal cadence

Quick internal note — copying Karthik so legal can draft language. Based on Jordan's feedback, commercial is comfortable with a compromise: 

- Auto-renew notice: 45 days (compromise).
- Termination for convenience: 30 days (Acme preference).
- Wind-down/data export: 30-day export window + 30-day support period for access (total 60 days operationally). Pro-rata refund for any prepaid committed capacity covering the remainder of the billing period.

We should also include: a) a short runbook appendix that confirms export formats (JSON/CSV), S3 temporary access patterns, and egress responsibility (default to customer unless contractually agreed otherwise), and b) the ability to request an extended export window for enterprise customers with a reasonable fee.

Karthik: can you draft a redline snippet that: replaces 60 days with 45 for auto-renew notice, sets termination-for-convenience to 30 days, and includes the two-runbook bullets above? If we can publically state the fallback (45/30/30) in the order form that should keep procurement happy and satisfy risk early.

Marcus
Head of Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Jordan Price <jordan.price@acmefin.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed termination workflow & renewal cadence
Attachments: suggested_clause_snippet.txt (text/plain)

Team / Jordan —

Below is a draft clause snippet intended for insertion into the Order Form / MSA that captures the 45/30/30 compromise Marcus suggested. Please treat as a draft — legal input welcome.

--- DRAFT SNIPPET START ---
Term and Renewal: The Initial Term is twelve (12) months. The Agreement shall automatically renew for successive twelve (12) month periods unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal at least forty-five (45) days prior to the end of the then-current Term.

Termination for Convenience: Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other party. Upon termination for convenience by Customer, Customer shall be entitled to a pro-rata refund of any prepaid, unused fees for the remainder of the then-current billing period.

Wind-Down and Data Export: Upon any termination, Redwood will provide Customer with a minimum thirty (30) day period to export Customer Data. During this period Redwood will provide reasonable access and support for export in commonly used formats (JSON and CSV). Customer is responsible for network egress costs unless otherwise agreed. Extended export windows may be available for an additional fee, subject to mutual agreement.
--- DRAFT SNIPPET END ---

Jordan — can you confirm if egress costs as default-to-customer is acceptable or if Acme requires we absorb egress for the first 30 days? If Acme needs us to cover egress for compliance reasons, flag and we'll escalate to pricing.

I'll attach this as suggested_clause_snippet.txt. If agreed, I'll update the redline doc and send back to you today for Acme's legal team.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel (Commercial Contracts)
